gate.how: node --experimental-strip-types, importing gateSense directly; all 61 rows passed through it
gate.result: 61/61 ok on the first pass, no repair round
gate.pre_write_check: A local re-implementation of the gate's level check was run over every sentence BEFORE the gate (rule A'1). It caught 18 defects (14 level drifts, 4 spelled-out numbers) that were fixed in the draft, which is why the gate itself saw zero failures.

spot_check.note: batch is smaller than 80, so every sense is marked spot_check=true

headword_source.why_not_canonical: TD-17 — newgeneralservicelist.com is not in this environment's egress allowlist. Unchanged from 2026-08-07.
headword_source.caveat: UNVERIFIED MIRROR: 2818 headwords vs NGSL v1.2's documented 2809. Only column 1 was read; the mirror's definitions were discarded unread and no definition was copied.
headword_source.provenance_note: No headword in this batch is a plausible mirror artefact: all 45 are high-frequency core English words. The 9 surplus entries, wherever they sit, are not in ranks 146-201.

selection_rule: ascending NGSL frequency rank, skipping any headword that already has a row in data/generated/. The four earlier batches covered 180 headwords across ranks 1-278; the 45 most frequent still-uncovered headwords are ranks 146-201.
selection_note: This is the first batch dominated by content words rather than grammar words: 36 of the 45 are nouns, verbs or adjectives. is_function_word is set per SENSE, not per headword — 'off' is an adverb in sense 1 (false, it is a predicative state word) and a preposition in sense 2 (true).
sense_policy: D-021 — one row per sense. 16 of the 45 headwords carry two senses (help, own, point, start, interest, old, off, live, end, while, kind, play, home, case, book, around), so 45 headwords produced 61 rows.
